before it ends.

value.name: Chinook music store
value.description: What the Chinook sample database means: a digital music store that sells tracks to customers in 24 countries. Each concept says what it is, the words people use for it, and which ModelSpec entity or property holds it, in which role. Concepts that are not specific to Chinook (country, currency, customer, invoice, price, revenue, date, population, per capita) are reused from the universal concepts at meaning://github.com/meaninggraph/core, each reference pinned to one commit with ?ref=.

sources.title: Population, total (World Development Indicators)
sources.note: Not part of Chinook. The latest observation per country. As of github.com/datatug/chinook-demo commit d2fc437 (data/geo/population_wb), the snapshot the DataTug Chinook demo uses, it is 2025 for all 24 Chinook countries.

concepts.description: A recording artist or band, known by its name.
An album by one artist, known by its title.

bindings.note: The album a track is on (the column allows none; every track in this data has one).

concepts.description: One audio or video track that the store sells, usually on an album.

bindings.note: The track bought on an invoice line.

concepts.description: The price of one copy of a track in the catalogue (0.99 or 1.99). The price actually charged is on the invoice line (see unit-price).
A music genre such as Rock or Jazz, assigned to tracks.
The file format of a track, such as "MPEG audio file" or "Protected AAC audio file".
A named list of tracks. A track can be on many playlists and a playlist holds many tracks; PlaylistTrack records which track is on which list.

bindings.note: Playlist membership, one row per track on a playlist.

concepts.description: A person who buys music from the store. Some customers name a company.

bindings.note: The customer who made a purchase.

concepts.description: The country in the customer's address, as Chinook spells it ("USA", "Czech Republic"). For questions about where music is bought, use billing-country instead.
A member of the store's staff. Employee.Title is the job title.
The employee someone reports to. Empty for the general manager.
The employee who looks after a customer.
One purchase by a customer: in Chinook every invoice is a completed order, so "purchase" and "order" name it too. Chinook has 412 invoices dated from 2021-01-01 to 2025-12-22.

bindings.note: The invoice a line is on.

concepts.description: The date of a purchase. The time part is always midnight.

The country an invoice is billed to, as Chinook spells it ("USA", "Czech Republic"). Use this one when a question asks which countries buy or spend: it is recorded on the sale itself, and it is the column the saved per-capita query groups by. In this data it equals the customer's country on every invoice, but it would stay right if a customer moved. Chinook's spellings are matched to countries by the labels and aliases of the universal country concept ("USA" is an alias of United States).
One track bought on an invoice.
The amount charged on an invoice. It equals the sum of UnitPrice x Quantity over the invoice's lines (true for all 412 invoices).
The price charged for one copy of a track on an invoice line.
Copies of a track bought on one invoice line (always 1 in Chinook).
Money the store took for music. The data names no currency; Chinook's prices (0.99 and 1.99) are read as US dollars.

measure.formula: The sum of Invoice.Total over the invoices in scope. Summing InvoiceLine.UnitPrice x InvoiceLine.Quantity over the same invoices' lines gives the same amount.

concepts.description: Not in Chinook. The population of each billing country, from the World Bank, matched to Chinook's country names through the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the universal country concept. A country without a population figure drops out of per-capita results.

measure.formula: The World Bank's latest total population of the country.

en: buy the most music relative to population

concepts.description: Music sales in a country divided by its population, per million people, so that small and large countries can be compared. Answers "Which countries buy the most music relative to their population?".

measure.formula: For each billing country: music sales divided by the country's population, multiplied by 1,000,000. The order is highest first.

value.name: Assets and finance
value.description: Value and money expressed as reusable concepts: currencies and amounts of money.

concepts.description: A unit of money used to express value, with an ISO 4217 code. Values are keyed by the lowercase alphabetic code. Starter subset: three currencies. No alias is a bare word or symbol that several currencies share ("dollar", "$"): the US dollar is "US dollar", "US dollars" or "US$", so another dollar can be added without a collision.

An amount of money. It is only meaningful together with its currency: its unit is one of the values of currency, so a concept that extends it states the currency as that value (unit: USD), and the check resolves the unit to exactly one currency. A dataset that does not store the currency must still say which one applies.

value.name: Calendar and time
value.description: Time concepts that keep their meaning across representations.

concepts.description: A calendar day: year, month and day, without a time of day. A dataset that stores a timestamp whose time is always midnight can treat it as a date. Questions that ask "when", "which year" or "which month" group by a date.

value.name: Commerce
value.description: Buying and selling: customers, invoices, prices and revenue.

concepts.description: A person or organization that purchases goods or services.

A request for payment for goods or services supplied to a customer: what was supplied, when, where it is billed, and the amount charged. Not an order (a request to supply) and not a receipt (proof of payment). A dataset whose invoices are purchases says so with its own synonyms.
One item on an invoice, with its unit price and quantity.
The amount charged on an invoice, normally the sum of its lines.
The amount asked for one unit of a product or service, such as the list price in a catalogue. The amount actually charged on a sale is a unit-price.
The price charged for one unit of an item on an invoice line.
How many units of an item were sold on one line.
The money received from sales over a period, before costs. From the buyer's side the same number is spend, so a question about who buys or spends the most asks for revenue grouped by the buyer.

measure.formula: The sum of the invoice totals of the sales in scope.

value.name: Geography
value.description: Places with a meaning shared across datasets: countries, cities, and the people who live in them. Starter subset: the country list holds a starter set of countries; the full ISO 3166-1 list comes later.

concepts.description: A country or territory with an ISO 3166-1 code, identified independently of any data source. Values are keyed by the lowercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. A dataset that stores a country by name matches it against a value's labels and aliases; one that stores a code matches it against the value's codes.

en: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

concepts.description: An ISO 3166-1 code that identifies a country: alpha-2 ("IE"), alpha-3 ("IRL") or numeric ("372"). Each country value lists all three.
A named settlement located within a country. No known values yet: city names repeat across countries, so a dataset matches a city together with its country.
The number of people living in a country at a point in time. Always state the year: populations change every year and sources differ.

measure.formula: The count of residents of the country in the stated year.

value.name: People and organizations
value.description: People, organizations, and the roles people hold in an organization.

concepts.description: A group with a defined identity and purpose, such as a company.
A person employed by an organization.
The employee that another employee reports to.

value.name: Statistics
value.description: Derived measures that apply to any dataset.

concepts.description: A pattern, not a number on its own: any measure for a place divided by the population of the same place, so that large and small places can be compared. It is a ratio, so it is never summed across places. A concept that extends it names the measure, the scale and the population source and year, and states its unit as the measure's unit per the scale's number of people (USD per million people).

measure.formula: The measure for a place, divided by the population of that place (same year where possible), multiplied by the scale (1 for "per person", 1,000,000 for "per million people").
